title: Extract Category Code from SKU
description:
Each product has a SKU in the format `CAT-###` where the first 3 characters are a category code. Write a query that returns `id`, `sku`, `name`, and the first 3 characters of the SKU as `category_code`.

**Table: products**

| Column | Type |
|--------|------|
| id | INT |
| sku | VARCHAR |
| name | VARCHAR |
schema_sql: CREATE TABLE products (id INT, sku VARCHAR, name VARCHAR); INSERT INTO products VALUES (1, 'ELC-001', 'Laptop'), (2, 'ELC-002', 'Smartphone'), (3, 'CLT-001', 'T-Shirt'), (4, 'CLT-002', 'Jeans'), (5, 'FRN-001', 'Chair'), (6, 'FRN-002', 'Desk'), (7, 'ELC-003', 'Headphones');
solution_sql: SELECT id, sku, name, SUBSTRING(sku, 1, 3) AS category_code FROM products

test_cases.description: Returns 7 rows with category_code as first 3 chars of sku

hints: `SUBSTRING(column, start, length)` extracts a portion of a string. The start position is 1-indexed.
You can also use `SUBSTR(sku, 1, 3)` — it is an alias for `SUBSTRING` in most databases.
explanation: `SUBSTRING(sku, 1, 3)` starts at position 1 and extracts 3 characters, giving us 'ELC', 'CLT', or 'FRN' as the category code from each SKU.
